title: Maps made of sticks and shells

probes.question: On a Marshallese stick chart, what represented island locations?
options: Shells tied to the framework, or lashed junctions of sticks

probes.question: True or false: Marshallese navigators consulted the stick chart during the trip.

image.alt: A Marshallese stick chart of thin bamboo ribs tied in a lattice with small white cowrie shells marking islands, on a dark blue background

body.question: Marshallese navigators made charts from coconut-frond midribs, with shells tied on. What did the charts show?
options: Major ocean swell patterns and how islands disrupt them
Where the best fishing spots were
Which islands belonged to which families
The names of every island in the Pacific
body.reveal: The charts represented major ocean swell patterns and the ways the islands disrupted those patterns. Island locations were represented by shells tied to the framework, or by the lashed junction of two or more sticks. The charts were studied and memorized prior to a voyage and were not consulted during a trip.
